- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

9	## Objective
10	
11	Route Hermes Knowledge Layer outputs (Spec 089) into Town as operator-facing
12	tasks, briefs, and alerts — without giving Town production mutation authority.
13	
14	```
15	Hermes  = source of truth / scheduler / repo-state brain
16	Town    = operator-facing assistant / inbox / task surface
17	Telegram = hard interrupt channel
18	Git/repo artifacts = permanent audit trail
19	```

21	---
22	
23	## Architecture
24	
25	Hermes generates deterministic artifacts. Town receives webhooks, creates tasks,
26	and surfaces summaries to the operator. Town does NOT control Hermes.
27	
28	### Data flow
29	
30	```
31	Hermes job completes
32	  → write ledger artifact (repo)
33	  → send_operator_event(channel="town", ...)
34	      → POST JSON to TOWN_WEBHOOK_URL
35	          → Town routine creates/updates task
36	          → Town DMs operator in Slack/email
37	```
38	
39	### What Town is NOT
40	
41	- NOT a scheduler
42	- NOT a cron controller
43	- NOT a repo mutator
44	- NOT a spec approver
45	- NOT allowed to reactivate bioshort_watch LLM
46	- NOT allowed to infer approval from a chat message
47	- NOT the authoritative source for any production state

51	## Integration path: email trigger (not webhook)
52	
53	Town does not currently expose a native inbound webhook endpoint.
54	The production-ready path today is email:
55	
56	  Hermes sends structured email to TOWN_EMAIL (djschulz@gmail.com)
57	  Town routine triggers on email arrival, filters on subject prefix [Hermes]
58	  Town creates task / DMs operator
59	
60	Subject format:
61	  [Hermes] {SEVERITY} | {event_type} | {title}
62	
63	Body: plain-text summary + JSON payload block (parseable by Town routine).
64	
65	Future: if Town adds native webhook support, operator_delivery.py can add
66	a _send_town_webhook() path alongside _send_town_email() with no callers
67	needing to change.

69	## Webhook payload schema (email body JSON block)
70	
71	All Hermes → Town events use this envelope:
72	
73	```json
74	{
75	  "data": {
76	    "source": "hermes",
77	    "event_type": "<event_type>",
78	    "severity": "INFO | WARN | FAIL",
79	    "title": "<human-readable title>",
80	    "artifact": "<relative repo path to ledger>",
81	    "summary": "<1-3 sentence plain-text summary>",
82	    "next_operator_action": "<specific next step, or 'none'>"
83	  }
84	}
85	```

24	    Town does not expose a native inbound webhook endpoint. The integration
25	    path is email: Hermes sends a structured email to TOWN_EMAIL; a Town
26	    routine triggers on arrival and creates a task.
27	
28	    Subject format: [Hermes] {SEVERITY} | {event_type} | {title}
29	    Town routine should filter on subject containing "[Hermes]".
30	
31	    Body: plain-text summary + JSON payload block for structured parsing.
32

36	                                 (default: djschulz@gmail.com)
37	    OPERATOR_DELIVERY_DRY_RUN  — "1" or "true" to log without sending
38	
39	    SMTP vars (shared with alert_email.py):
40	    SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD
41	
42	Behaviour
43	---------
44	    - dry_run=True (or OPERATOR_DELIVERY_DRY_RUN=1): logs payload, skips send, returns True.
45	    - Missing SMTP creds: logs warning, returns False, never raises.
46	    - SMTP errors: logged at WARNING level, returns False, never raises.
47	    - Deduplication: uses common/alert_dedupe.py (same store as alerts.py).
48	      Dedupe window: 1 hour for INFO, 30 min for WARN, 15 min for FAIL.
49	    - channel="telegram": delegates to common/alerts.py send_operator_alert().
50	    - channel="slack": not yet implemented (logs warning, returns False).

54	    Spec 090 — Town-Hermes Bridge, Phase A
55	    specs/changes/spec_090_town_hermes_bridge.md
56	
57	Guardrails
58	----------
59	    This module sends read-only summaries and artifact paths only.
60	    It does NOT grant Town write access to repo, cron, config, or scoring.
61	    It does NOT infer operator approval from any delivery response.
62	"""

65	
66	import json
67	import logging
68	import os

70	from typing import Any, Optional
71	
72	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
73

76	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	
78	SEVERITY_EMOJI = {
79	    "FAIL": "🔴",
80	    "WARN": "🟡",
81	    "INFO": "🔵",
82	}
83	
84	DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS = {
85	    "FAIL": 900,

95	
96	
97	def _env(key: str, default: str = "") -> str:

99	
100	
101	def _is_dry_run(override: Optional[bool]) -> bool:
102	    if override is not None:
103	        return override
104	    return _env("OPERATOR_DELIVERY_DRY_RUN", "1").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")

108	# Build structured payload (shared across channels)
109	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

111	
112	def _build_payload(
113	    *,
114	    severity: str,
115	    event_type: str,
116	    title: str,
117	    summary: str,
118	    artifact: str,
119	    next_operator_action: str,
120	    extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]],
121	) -> dict[str, Any]:
122	    data: dict[str, Any] = {

124	        "event_type": event_type,
125	        "severity": severity,
126	        "title": title,
127	        "summary": summary,
128	        "artifact": artifact,
129	        "next_operator_action": next_operator_action,
130	        "as_of": datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),

132	    if extra:

142	def _send_town_email(

146	    title: str,
147	    subject_title: str,
148	    summary: str,
149	    artifact: str,

151	    extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]],

155	    payload = _build_payload(

157	        event_type=event_type,
158	        title=title,
159	        summary=summary,
160	        artifact=artifact,

162	        extra=extra,
163	    )
164	
165	    to_addr = _env("TOWN_EMAIL", TOWN_EMAIL_DEFAULT)
166	    # Clean subject: [Hermes] {SEVERITY} | {event_type} | {original caller title}
167	    subject = f"[Hermes] {severity} | {event_type} | {subject_title}"

174	    ]

224	        message = f"{title}\n{summary}" if summary else title
225	        if dry_run:

228	                severity,
229	                event_type,
230	                message,
231	            )
232	            return True

235	            system=f"hermes:{event_type}",
236	            message=message,
237	            dedupe_key=dedupe_key,
238	        )

241	        return False

243	
244	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
245	# Deduplication
246	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
247	
248	
249	def _is_duplicate(event_type: str, severity: str) -> bool:
250	    try:
251	        from common.alert_dedupe import AlertDedupeStore
252	
253	        window = DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS.get(severity, 3600)
254	        store = AlertDedupeStore()
255	        key = f"operator_delivery:{event_type}"
256	        if store.is_duplicate(key, window_seconds=window):
257	            return True
258	        store.record(key)
259	        return False
260	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
261	        return False
262	
263	
264	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
265	# Public interface
266	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
267	
268	
269	def send_operator_event(
270	    channel: str,
271	    severity: str,
272	    event_type: str,
273	    title: str,
274	    summary: str = "",
275	    artifact: str = "",
276	    next_operator_action: str = "none",
277	    extra: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
278	    dry_run: Optional[bool] = None,
279	    skip_dedupe: bool = False,
280	) -> bool:
281	    """
282	    Route a Hermes Knowledge Layer event to the operator.
283	
284	    Parameters
285	    ----------
286	    channel : "town" | "telegram" | "slack"
287	        Delivery channel.
288	        "town"     — structured email to TOWN_EMAIL (Town routine trigger).
289	        "telegram" — Telegram alert via common/alerts.py.
290	        "slack"    — not yet implemented.
291	    severity : "INFO" | "WARN" | "FAIL"
292	    event_type : str
293	        Machine-readable event identifier.
294	        Examples: "held_spec_ledger", "first_fire_fail", "snapshot_missing".
295	    title : str
296	        Short human-readable title (email subject / notification subject).
297	    summary : str
298	        1-3 sentence plain-text summary. Optional.
299	    artifact : str
300	        Relative repo path to the source ledger artifact. Optional.
301	    next_operator_action : str
302	        Specific next step for the operator, or "none".
303	    extra : dict | None
304	        Additional fields to include in the JSON payload.
305	    dry_run : bool | None
306	        Override dry-run mode. None = read OPERATOR_DELIVERY_DRY_RUN env.
307	    skip_dedupe : bool
308	        If True, bypass deduplication (use for forced re-alerts or tests).
309	
310	    Returns
311	    -------
312	    bool
313	        True if delivered (or dry-run logged), False if skipped/failed.
314	    """
315	    dry = _is_dry_run(dry_run)
316	
317	    emoji = SEVERITY_EMOJI.get(severity.upper(), "⚪")
318	    # Build a display title with emoji prefix (used in JSON payload + logs)
319	    # Keep the original caller title for use in email subjects
320	    original_title = title
321	    if not title.startswith(emoji):
322	        title = f"{emoji} {severity} | {event_type} | {title}"
323	
324	    if not skip_dedupe and _is_duplicate(event_type, severity):
325	        logger.debug("[operator_delivery] dedupe skip: %s/%s", channel, event_type)
326	        return False
327	
328	    if channel == "town":
329	        return _send_town_email(
330	            severity=severity,
331	            event_type=event_type,
332	            title=title,
333	            subject_title=original_title,
334	            summary=summary,
335	            artifact=artifact,
336	            next_operator_action=next_operator_action,
337	            extra=extra,
338	            dry_run=dry,
339	        )
340	
341	    if channel == "telegram":
342	        return _send_telegram(
343	            severity=severity,
344	            event_type=event_type,
345	            title=title,
346	            summary=summary,
347	            dry_run=dry,
348	        )
349	
350	    if channel == "slack":
351	        logger.warning("[operator_delivery] slack channel not yet implemented")
352	        return False
353	
354	    logger.warning("[operator_delivery] unknown channel: %s", channel)
355	    return False
